question: What is the short title of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972?
answer: Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972.
required_evidence: These rules may be called the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972.

question: On what date did the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972 come into force?
answer: 1st June, 1972.
required_evidence: They shall come into force on the \(1^{\mathrm{st}}\) day of June, 1972.

question: Which categories of Government servants are expressly excluded from the application of these rules?
answer: Railway servants; persons in casual or daily-rated or part-time employment; persons paid from contingencies; workmen employed in industrial establishments; persons employed in work-charged establishments; members of the All India Services; persons locally recruited for service in Diplomatic, Consular or other Indian establishments in foreign countries; persons employed on contract except when the contract provides otherwise; persons in respect of whom special provisions have been made by or under the Constitution or any other law; persons governed by the Fundamental Rules or the Civil Service Regulations; persons serving under a Central Government Department on deputation from a State Government or any other source for a limited duration.
required_evidence: (a) Railway servants;
(b) persons in casual or daily-rated or part-time employment;
(c) persons paid from contingencies;
(d) workmen employed in industrial establishments;
(e) persons employed in work-charged establishments;
(f) members of the All India Services;
(g) persons locally recruited for service in Diplomatic, Consular or other Indian establishments in foreign countries;
(h) persons employed on contract except when the contract provides otherwise;
(i) persons in respect of whom special provisions have been made by or under the provisions of the Constitution or any other law for the time being in force;
(j) persons governed, for purposes of leave, by the Fundamental Rules or the Civil Service Regulations;
(k) persons serving under a Central Government Department, on deputation from a State Government or any other source, for a limited duration.

question: What does the term Administrator mean under these rules?
answer: An Administrator of a Union Territory.
required_evidence: "Administrator" means an Administrator of a Union Territory;

question: What is the meaning of Audit Officer in these rules?
answer: The Accounts and Audit Officer, whatever his official designation, in whose circle the office of the Government servant is situated.
required_evidence: "Audit Officer" means the Accounts and Audit Officer, whatever his official designation, in whose circle the office of the Government servant is situated;

question: How is the authority competent to grant leave defined?
answer: The authority specified in Column (3) of the First Schedule to these rules, competent to grant the kind of leave specified in the corresponding entries in Column (2) of the said Schedule.
required_evidence: "Authority competent to grant leave" means the authority specified in Column (3) of the First Schedule to these rules, competent to grant the kind of leave specified in the corresponding entries in Column (2) of the said Schedule;

question: What is included in completed years of service or one year's continuous service?
answer: Continuous service of specified duration under the Central Government and includes the period spent on duty as well as on leave including extraordinary leave.
required_evidence: "Completed years of service" or "one year's continuous service" means continuous service of specified duration under the Central Government and includes the period spent on duty as well as on leave including extraordinary leave;

question: What is the date of retirement in relation to a Government servant?
answer: The afternoon of the last day of the month in which the Government servant attains the age prescribed for retirement under the terms and conditions governing his services.
required_evidence: "Date of retirement" or "date of his retirement" in relation to a Government servant, means the afternoon of the last day of the month in which the Government servant attains the age prescribed for retirement under the terms and conditions governing his services.

question: What does Department of the Central Government include?
answer: A Ministry or a Department of the Central Government as notified from time to time and includes the Planning Commission, the Department of Parliamentary Affairs, the President's Secretariat, the Vice-President's Secretariat, the Cabinet Secretariat and the Prime Minister's Secretariat.
required_evidence: "Department of the Central Government" means a Ministry or a Department of the Central Government as notified from time to time and includes the Planning Commission, the Department of Parliamentary Affairs, the President's Secretariat, the Vice-President's Secretariat, the Cabinet Secretariat and the Prime Minister's Secretariat;

question: What does disability mean under these rules?
answer: Specified disability, benchmark disability and disability having high support needs as referred to in the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (49 of 2016).
required_evidence: "disability" means "specified disability", "benchmark disability" and "disability having high support needs" as referred to in the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (49 of 2016).

question: What is foreign service according to these rules?
answer: Service in which a Government servant receives his pay with the sanction of Government from any source other than the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of any State or the Consolidated Fund of a Union Territory.
required_evidence: "Foreign service" means service in which a Government servant receives his pay with the sanction of Government from any source other than the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of any State [or the Consolidated Fund of a Union Territory];

question: What is meant by Form in these rules?
answer: A Form appended to the Second Schedule to these rules.

question: Who is a Government servant in quasi-permanent employ?
answer: An officer who, having been declared by the Union Public Service Commission to be eligible for appointment to the ministerial Services of the Government of India, has been appointed to a temporary or officiating vacancy on the understanding given to him in writing before he took up the appointment, that that vacancy is expected to become permanent but is not confirmed after completion of three years continuous service; or an officer who may be declared as quasi-permanent under the Central Civil Services (Temporary Services) Rules, 1965.
required_evidence: "Government servant in quasi-permanent employ" means

(A) an officer who, having been declared by the Union Public Service Commission to be eligible for appointment to the ministerial Services of the Government of India, has been appointed to a temporary or officiating vacancy on the understanding given to him in writing before he took up the appointment, that that vacancy is expected to become permanent but is not confirmed after completion of three years continuous service;
(B) an officer who may be declared as quasi-permanent under the Central Civil Services (Temporary Services) Rules, 1965.

question: Who is a Government servant in permanent employ?
answer: An officer who holds substantively or provisionally substantively a permanent post or who holds a lien on a permanent post or who would have held a lien on permanent post had the lien not been suspended.

question: What does Head of Mission mean?

question: Who is a Military Officer under these rules?
answer: An officer of the Armed Forces who is a Commissioned Officer of the Army, the Navy or the Air Force, or a Junior Commissioned Officer including an honorary commissioned officer, or an other rank of the Army, or a Branch List Officer or rating of the Navy, or an airman including a Master Warrant Officer of the Air Force.

(i) a Commissioned Officer of the Army, the Navy or the Air Force, or

question: What is a Vacation Department?
answer: A department or part of a department, to which regular vacations are allowed, during which Government servants serving in the department are permitted to be absent from duty.
required_evidence: "Vacation Department" means a department or part of a department, to which regular vacations are allowed, during which Government servants serving in the department are permitted to be absent from duty.

question: Do these rules continue to govern Government servants on temporary transfer to Indian Railways or a State Government or on foreign service within India?
answer: Yes, they shall continue to be governed by these rules.

question: To what extent do these rules apply to Government servants on foreign service outside India or on temporary transfer to the Armed Forces of the Union?

question: When a permanent Government servant to whom these rules do not apply is transferred temporarily to a service or post to which these rules apply, which leave rules remain applicable to him?

question: Can leave be claimed as a matter of right?

question: How is a Government servant's claim to leave regulated?

question: What is the effect of dismissal, removal or resignation on leave at credit?
answer: Except as provided in Rule 39 and this rule, any claim to leave to the credit of a Government servant who is dismissed or removed or who resigns from Government service ceases from the date of such dismissal or removal or resignation.
required_evidence: Except as provided in Rule 39 and this rule, any claim to leave to the credit of a Government servant, who is dismissed or removed or who resigns from Government service, ceases from the date of such dismissal or removal or resignation.

question: If a Government servant applies for another post under Government of India through proper channel and is required to resign his post before taking up the new one, does his leave at credit lapse?

question: A Government servant who is dismissed or removed from service and is reinstated on appeal or revision is entitled to count what for leave?

question: A Government servant who retired on compensation or invalid pension or gratuity and is re-employed and allowed to count past service for pension is entitled to count what towards leave?

question: Can a Government servant claim commutation of one kind of leave into another as a matter of right?

question: What must a Medical Authority certify in Form 3-A in case of a Government servant who has acquired disability?

question: How shall leave be treated when the production of a medical certificate has been waived?
answer: It shall not be treated as leave on medical certificate and shall be debited against leave other than leave on medical grounds.
required_evidence: Such leave shall not, however, be treated as leave on medical certificate and shall be debited against leave other than leave on medical grounds.

question: Who may waive the application of Clause (a) of the proviso to Rule 22(1) on condition that the departing Government servant remains responsible for moneys in his charge?
answer: The Head of Department.
required_evidence: On condition that the departing Government servant remains responsible for the moneys in this charge, the Head of Department may, in any particular case, waive the application of Clause (a) of the proviso to subrule (1).

question: If holidays are prefixed to leave, from when do the leave and any consequent rearrangement of pay and allowances take effect?
answer: From the day after the holidays.
required_evidence: if holidays are prefixed to leave, the leave and any consequent rearrangement of pay and allowances take effect from the day after the holidays; and

question: If holidays are suffixed to leave, from when is the leave treated as having terminated and pay and allowances rearranged?
answer: From the day on which the leave would have ended if holidays had not been suffixed.
required_evidence: if holidays are suffixed to leave, the leave is treated as having terminated and any consequent rearrangement of pay and allowances take effect from the day on which the leave would have ended if holidays had not been suffixed.

question: What may be treated as a holiday for the purpose of combining holidays with leave under Rule 22?
answer: A compensatory leave granted in lieu of duty performed by a Government servant on Sunday or a holiday for a full day.
required_evidence: A compensatory leave granted in lieu of duty performed by a Government servant on Sunday or a holiday for a full day may be treated as a holiday for the above purpose.

question: When a Government servant is recalled to duty from leave in India, from what date is he treated as on duty and what is he entitled to draw?
answer: He is treated as on duty from the date on which he starts for the station to which he is ordered, and is entitled to travelling allowance for the journey and leave salary until he joins his post at the same rate as but for recall.
required_evidence: if the leave from which he is recalled is in India, to be treated as on duty from the date on which he starts for the station to which he is ordered, and to draw - (i) travelling allowance under rules made in this behalf for the journey; and (ii) leave salary, until he joins his post, at the same rate at which he would have drawn it but for recall to duty;

question: When a Government servant is recalled from leave out of India, under what condition is he entitled to refund of his passage from India?
answer: If he has not completed half the period of his leave by the date of leaving for India on recall or three months, whichever is shorter.
required_evidence: refund of his passage from India if he has not completed half the period of his leave by the date of leaving for India on recall or three months, whichever is shorter;

question: Can a Government servant on leave preparatory to retirement return to duty without consent?
answer: No, he is precluded from returning to duty save with the consent of the authority competent to appoint him to the post from which he proceeded on leave preparatory to retirement.
required_evidence: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (1), a Government servant on leave preparatory to retirement shall be precluded from returning to duty, save with the consent of the authority competent to appoint him to the post from which he proceeded on leave preparatory to retirement.

question: From whom must a Gazetted officer obtain a medical certificate of fitness to return to duty?
answer: From a Medical Board, except in specified cases.
required_evidence: If the Government servant is a gazetted officer the certificate under clause (a) shall be obtained from a Medical Board, except in the following cases:- (i) Cases in which the leave is for not more than three months; (ii) Cases in which leave is for more than three months or leave for three months or less is extended beyond three months, and the medical Board states, at the time of granting the original certificate or the certificate for extension, that the Government servant need not appear before another Medical Board for obtaining the certificate of fitness.

question: Who may sign the fitness certificate for a non-Gazetted Government servant returning from leave?
answer: A Registered Medical Practitioner.
required_evidence: In the case of a non-Gazetted Government servant, the authority under which the Government servant is employed on return from leave may, in its discretion, accept a certificate signed by a Registered Medical Practitioner.

question: Is a Government servant returning from leave entitled to resume the post he held before going on leave as a matter of course?
answer: No, he is not entitled in the absence of specific orders to that effect.
required_evidence: A Government servant returning from leave is not entitled, in the absence of specific orders to that effect, to resume as a matter of course the post which he held before going on leave.

question: What note is given regarding a Government servant who had been suffering from Tuberculosis?
answer: He may be allowed to resume duty on the basis of a fitness certificate which recommends light work for him.
required_evidence: A Government servant who had been suffering from Tuberculosis may be allowed to resume duty on the basis of fitness certificate which recommends light work for him.

question: What is the consequence of wilful absence from duty after the expiry of leave?
answer: It renders a Government servant liable to disciplinary action.
required_evidence: Wilful absence from duty after the expiry of leave renders a Government servant liable to disciplinary action.

question: What is credited to the leave account of a Government servant not in permanent employ who is appointed substantively to a permanent post without interruption of service?
answer: The earned leave which would have been admissible if his previous duty had been rendered as a Government servant in permanent employ, diminished by any earned leave already taken.
required_evidence: Where a Government servant not in permanent employ or quasi- permanent employ is appointed without interruption of service substantively to a permanent post or declared as quasi permanent, his leave account shall be credited with the earned leave which would have been admissible, if his previous duty had been rendered as a Government servant in permanent employ diminished by any earned leave already taken.

question: Into what may extraordinary leave be converted when a Government servant had availed it since the date of permanent or quasi-permanent appointment?
answer: It may be converted into earned leave to the extent it is due and admissible as a result of recasting of his leave account.
required_evidence: Where a Government servant had availed of extraordinary leave since the date of permanent appointment or quasi- permanent appointment, such leave may, subject to the provisions of rule 10, be converted into earned leave to the extent it is due and admissible as a result of recasting of his leave account.

question: When does a period spent in foreign service count as duty for the purpose of earned leave under Rule 26?
answer: If contribution towards leave salary is paid on account of such period.
required_evidence: A period spent in foreign service shall count as duty for purposes of this rule, if contribution towards leave salary is paid on account of such period.

question: What is the earned leave admissible to a Government servant of non-Asiatic domicile recruited in India before 1st February, 1949 and entitled to leave passage?
answer: One-seventh of the period spent on duty, and he ceases to earn such leave when the earned leave due amounts to 180 days.
required_evidence: The earned leave admissible to a Government servant of non- Asiatic domicile recruited in India, who is in continuous service from a date prior to the 1st February, 1949 and is entitled to leave passage, is one- seventh of the period spent on duty and he ceases to earn such leave when the earned leave due amounts to 180 days.

question: How are fractions of a day rounded off while affording credit of earned leave?
answer: To the nearest day.
required_evidence: While affording credit of earned leave, fractions of a day shall be rounded off to the nearest day.

question: If a Government servant serving in a Vacation Department does not avail any vacation in a year, how is earned leave calculated?
answer: As per Rule 26 instead of Clauses (a) and (b).
required_evidence: If, in any year, the Government servant does not avail any vacation, earned leave will be as per Rule 26 instead of Clauses (a) and (b).

question: What is the limit on total duration of vacation and earned leave taken in conjunction under Rule 28?
answer: It shall not exceed the amount of earned leave due and admissible at a time under Rule 26.
required_evidence: Provided that the total duration of vacation and earned leave taken in conjunction, whether the earned leave is taken in combination with or in continuation of other leave or not, shall not exceed the amount of earned leave due and admissible to the Government at a time under Rule 26.

question: What is the entitlement of a Government servant eligible for Departmental leave under Rule 49?
answer: Half pay leave of twenty days on completion of twelve months of actual duty.
required_evidence: A Government servant who is eligible for Departmental leave under Rule 49, shall be entitled to half pay leave of twenty days on completion of twelve months of actual duty.

question: On what grounds may half pay leave be granted under Rule 29?
answer: On medical certificate or on private affairs.
required_evidence: The leave under this rule may be granted on medical certificate or on private affairs.

question: If a Government servant who has been granted commuted leave resigns without returning to duty, how is the commuted leave treated?
answer: It shall be treated as half pay leave and the difference between leave salary for commuted leave and half pay leave shall be recovered.
required_evidence: Where a Government servant who has been granted commuted leave resigns from service or at his request permitted to retire voluntarily without returning to duty, the commuted leave shall be treated as half pay leave and the difference between the leave salary in respect of commuted leave and half pay leave shall be recovered:

question: What happens if a Government servant who has been granted Leave Not Due resigns without returning to duty?
answer: The Leave Not Due shall be cancelled, his resignation or retirement takes effect from the date the leave commenced, and the leave salary shall be recovered.
required_evidence: Where a Government servant who has been granted Leave Not Due resigns form service or at his request permitted to retire voluntarily without returning to duty, the Leave Not Due shall be cancelled, his resignation or retirement taking effect from the date on which such leave had commenced, and the leave salary shall be recovered.

question: Which Government servants may be granted extraordinary leave for attending the Pre-Examination Training Course?
answer: Government servants belonging to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled Tribes.
required_evidence: Government servants belonging to the Scheduled Castes or the Scheduled tribes may, for the purpose of attending the Pre- Examination Training Course at the centers notified by the Government from time to time, be granted extraordinary leave by Head of Department in relaxation of the provisions of sub-rule (2).

question: How are two spells of extraordinary leave treated if intervened by any other kind of leave?
answer: They shall be treated as one continuous spell of extraordinary leave for the purposes of sub-rule (2).
required_evidence: Two spells of extraordinary leave, if intervened by any other kind of leave, shall be treated as one continuous spell of extraordinary leave for the purposes of sub-rule (2).

question: What may the authority competent to grant leave commute retrospectively?
answer: Periods of absence without leave into extraordinary leave.
required_evidence: The authority competent to grant leave may commute retrospectively periods of absence without leave into extraordinary leave.

question: If it is proposed to terminate the services of a probationer, beyond what date shall any leave granted to him not extend?
answer: It shall not extend beyond the date on which the probationary period as already sanctioned or extended expires, or beyond any earlier date on which his services are terminated by order of the appointing authority.
required_evidence: If, for any reason, it is proposed to terminate the services of a probationer, any leave which may be granted to him shall not extend - (i) beyond the date on which the probationary period as already sanctioned or extended expires, or (ii) beyond any earlier date on which his services are terminated by the orders of an authority competent to appoint him.

question: How is a person appointed to a post on probation entitled to leave under these rules?
answer: As a temporary or a permanent Government servant according as his appointment is against a temporary or a permanent post.
required_evidence: A person appointed to a post on probation shall be entitled to leave under these rules as a temporary or a permanent Government servant according as his appointment is against a temporary or a permanent post:

question: Who decides whether to grant or refuse leave preparatory to retirement to a Government servant on foreign service in a local body?
answer: The foreign employer with the concurrence of the lending authority under the Central Government.
required_evidence: Where a Government servant who is on foreign service in or under any Local Authority or a Corporation or Company wholly or substantially owned or controlled by the Government or a Body controlled or financed by the Government (hereinafter referred to as the local body) applies for leave preparatory to retirement, the decision to grant or refuse such leave shall be taken by foreign employer with the concurrence of the lending authority under Central Government.

question: When is leave preparatory to retirement admissible to a Government servant on foreign service under a local body other than the one mentioned in Rule 38(2)(a)?
answer: Only when he quits duty under the foreign employer.
required_evidence: Where a Government servant is on foreign service in or under a local body other than the one mentioned in Clause (a) of sub-rule (2), leave preparatory to retirement shall be admissible to him only when he quits duty under the foreign employer:

question: Under what circumstances may the authority competent to grant leave withhold whole or part of cash equivalent of earned leave on retirement?
answer: If the Government servant retires while under suspension or while disciplinary or criminal proceedings are pending, and there is a possibility of money becoming recoverable from him.
required_evidence: The authority competent to grant leave may withhold whole or part of cash equivalent of earned leave in the case of a Government servant who retires from service on attaining the age of retirement while under suspension or while disciplinary or criminal proceedings are pending against him, if in the view of such authority there is a possibility of some money becoming recoverable from him on conclusion of the proceedings against him on conclusion of the proceedings, he will become eligible to the amount so withheld after adjustment of Government dues, if any.

question: During the period of extension of service beyond retirement in public interest, what earned leave may be granted?
answer: Any earned leave due in respect of the period of extension plus the earned leave at credit on the date of retirement, subject to a maximum of 180 days or 300 days as prescribed in Rule 26.
required_evidence: Where the service of a Government servant has been extended, in the interest of public service beyond the date of his retirement, he may be granted - (i) during the period of extension, any earned leave due in respect of the period of such extension plus the earned leave which was at his credit on the date of his retirement subject to a maximum of 180 days / 300 days as the case may be, as prescribed in Rule 26.
